AMZN.rationale: Amazon demonstrates strong fundamental health and positive trajectory across its key segments. Q1 2026 results showed 17% revenue growth to $181.5B, with AWS accelerating to 28% YoY growth (fastest in 15 quarters), advertising up 22%, and operating income growing 30%. The quarterly trajectory shows consistent improvement: revenue from $155.67B (Q1) to $167.70B (Q2) to $180.17B (Q3), with EPS rising from $1.59 to $1.68 to $1.95. Balance sheet is solid with $369.6B equity, $55.1B debt, and debt-to-equity of just 0.149. However, valuation is elevated: P/E of 38.5x sits near the top of its 365-day range (28.2-39.0), and P/B of 7.96 is also near highs (5.8-8.3). The stock has rallied 21.8% in the last quarter alone, pricing in much of the positive momentum. The $200B capex commitment for 2026 compresses free cash flow dramatically (FCF fell to $1.2B TTM per CNBC), creating real near-term financial constraints. Regulatory risks from the California antitrust lawsuit and FTC action add uncertainty. The Q1 earnings beat and AWS reacceleration provide a near-term positive catalyst, but the stock's sharp recent rally and rich valuation temper the upside. Net margin has improved to 11.1% from 10.1% a year ago, and ROE remains healthy at 20.7%, supporting the positive fundamental view.
